'''Eileen Minnie Brooke''' (1905 – 1989) was a British [[statistician]] and health policy professional.

== Education ==
Eileen Minnie Brooke attended [[History of Queen Mary University of London|East London College]], earning a B.Sc. in mathematics in 1926, and an M.Sc. in mathematics in 1929. She completed doctoral studies in 1952.<ref name=":3">[https://aim25.com/cgi-bin/vcdf/detail?coll_id=10720&inst_id=39&nv1=browse&nv2=repos Eileen Minnie Brooke (-1989) papers], Queen Mary University of London.</ref>

== In Great Britain, 1940s–1960s ==
In the 1940s, Brooke was based at the [[Emergency Hospital Service|Emergency Medical Service]] Statistical Branch in Norcross, and studied wartime health issues, including battle exhaustion,<ref name=":1" /> burns,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Brooke|first=Eileen M.|date=1945|title=Burns And Their Treatment Among E.M.S. Hospital In-Patients|journal=The British Medical Journal|volume=1|issue=4390|pages=259–260|jstor=20347818|issn=0007-1447}}</ref> and [[Peptic ulcer disease|gastric ulcers]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Brooke|first=Eileen M.|date=1950|title=Relative Incidence Of Gastric And Duodenal Ulcers|journal=The British Medical Journal|volume=2|issue=4678|pages=560–561|doi=10.1136/bmj.2.4678.560|jstor=25358267|pmid=15434458|pmc=2038276|issn=0007-1447}}</ref>  She was elected a fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] in 1943.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1943|title=Newly elected fellows of the Society|journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society|volume=106|issue=1|pages=30|doi=10.2307/2980239|jstor=2980239|issn=0952-8385}}</ref>

In the 1950s, Brooke was a statistician in the [[Medical statistics|Medical Statistics]] branch of the [[General Register Office for England and Wales|General Register Office]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9XcYAAAAMAAJ&q=%22E.%20M.%20Brooke%22%20statistician&pg=PA308|title=The Registrar-General's Statistical Review of England and Wales|date=1954|publisher=H.M. Stationery Office|pages=308|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9XcYAAAAMAAJ&q=%22Miss%20E.%20Brooke%22%20statistics&pg=PA309|title=The Registrar-General's Statistical Review of England and Wales|date=1954|publisher=H.M. Stationery Office|pages=309|language=en}}</ref> She attended the Second [[World Psychiatric Association|World Congress of Psychiatry]] in [[Zürich]] in 1957, and presented a paper on [[schizophrenia]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=General Register Office|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FoMYAAAAMAAJ&q=%22Miss+E.+M.+Brooke%22&pg=RA3-PA215|title=The Registrar-General's Statistical Review of England and Wales|date=1958|publisher=H.M. Stationery Office|pages=215|language=en}}</ref> She also attended the [[World Federation for Mental Health|International Congress on Mental Health]] in Paris in 1961.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Office|first=Great Britain General Register|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2qoXAAAAMAAJ&q=%22Miss%20Brooke%22%20%22World%20Health%20Organization%22&pg=RA2-PA309|title=The Registrar-General's Statistical Review of England and Wales|date=1963|publisher=H.M. Stationery Office|language=en}}</ref>

Brooke was co-author of ''The survey of sickness, 1943 to 1952'' (1957, with W. P. D. Logan),<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Logan|first1=W. P. D|title=The survey of sickness, 1943 to 1952|last2=Brooke|first2=Eileen M|date=1957|publisher=H.M. Stationery Off.|location=London|language=en|oclc=504143}}</ref> and author of ''A cohort study of patients first admitted to mental hospitals in 1954 and 1955'' (1963)<ref>{{Cite book|last=Brooke|first=Eileen M|title=A cohort study of patients first admitted to mental hospitals in 1954 and 1955.|date=1963|publisher=H.M. Stationery Off.|location=London|language=en|oclc=536223}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zOthAAAAIAAJ&q=%22Eileen%20M.%20Brooke%22&pg=PA367|title=The Registrar General's Statistical Review of England and Wales. [New Annual Series]|date=1962|pages=367|language=en}}</ref> and ''A census of patients in psychiatric beds, 1963'' (1967).<ref>{{Cite book|last=Brooke|first=Eileen M|title=A census of patients in psychiatric beds, 1963|date=1967|publisher=H.M.S.O.|location=London|language=en|oclc=957614}}</ref>

== International work, 1960s–1970s ==
Brooke spoke at a mental health conference in Pennsylvania in 1964.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/47382457/mental-health-conference-planned-at/|title=Mental Health Conference Planned at Pocono Manor|date=1964-04-22|work=Wilkes-Barre Times Leader, the Evening News, Wilkes-Barre Record|access-date=2020-03-26|pages=10|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> She was chief of the Department of Medical Information and Statistics at the University Institute of Social and Preventive Medicine in [[Lausanne]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Raeburn|first=H. B.|date=1980-08-01|title=Book Reviews|url=https://academic.oup.com/jpubhealth/article/2/3/267/1554152|journal=Journal of Public Health|language=en|volume=2|issue=3|pages=267|doi=10.1093/oxfordjournals.pubmed.a043342|issn=1741-3842|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name=":2">''[http://aei.pitt.edu/43422/1/A6208.pdf Seminar of the Medico-Social Risks of Alcohol Consumption]'' (World Health Organization, Luxembourg, 1977): 4, 163, 218.</ref> She was a collaborating investigator on the [[World Health Organization]]'s International Pilot Study of Schizophrenia in the late 1960s.<ref>''[https://apps.who.int/iris/bitstream/handle/10665/37767/WHO_PHP_63.pdf?sequence=1 Schizophrenia: A Multinational Study]'' (World Health Organization 1975): 3.</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sartorius|first1=N.|last2=Shapiro|first2=R.|last3=Kimura|first3=M.|last4=Barrett|first4=K.|date=November 1972|title=WHO International Pilot Study of Schizophrenia1|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/psychological-medicine/article/who-international-pilot-study-of-schizophrenia1/F669EEDC4A065A453A865D5F28877167|journal=Psychological Medicine|language=en|volume=2|issue=4|pages=422–425|doi=10.1017/S0033291700045244|pmid=4656537|s2cid=41342582 |issn=1469-8978|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1977 she spoke at an WHO workshop on "the medico-social risks of alcohol consumption" in Luxembourg.<ref name=":2" />

Brooke wrote and edited policy reports for the World Health Organization and other international bodies, including ''The methodology of psychiatric out-patient data collection'' (1973),<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Brooke|first1=Eileen M|title=The methodology of psychiatric out-patient data collection; report on a pilot study undertaken for the Regional Office for Europe of the World Health Organization.|last2=World Health Organization|last3=Regional Office for Europe|date=1973|publisher=Distributed by the Regional Office for Europe, World Health Organization|location=Copenhagen|language=en|oclc=8360119}}</ref> ''The current and future use of registers in health information systems'' (1974),<ref>{{Cite book|last=Brooke, Eileen M.|title=The current and future use of registers in health information systems|date=1974|publisher=World Health Organization|isbn=92-4-170008-4|location=Geneva|oclc=1074055}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Mowbray|first=Derek|date=1975-06-01|title=Book Reviews|url=https://academic.oup.com/ije/article/4/2/147/808951|journal=International Journal of Epidemiology|language=en|volume=4|issue=2|pages=147|doi=10.1093/ije/4.2.147|issn=0300-5771|url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''Suicide and attempted suicide'' (1974),<ref>{{Cite book|last=Brooke|first=Eileen M|title=Suicide and attempted suicide|journal=Public Health Papers|date=1974|issue=58|pages=5–127|publisher=World Health Organization|isbn=978-92-4-130058-2|location=Geneva|pmid=4479495|language=en|oclc=1102693}}</ref> and ''Activities in the field of drug dependence (European region)'' (1975).<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Brooke|first1=Eileen M|title=Activities in the field of drug dependence (European region)|last2=Council of Europe|last3=Committee of Ministers|date=1975|publisher=Council of Europe, Public Health Division, Ad hoc Committee on Drug Dependence|location=Strasbourg|language=en|oclc=2128439}}</ref>

== Death ==
Brooke died in 1989. A colleague wrote in an obituary that "Miss Brooke was precious to WHO's programmes because she was a statistician who liked to assemble data, enjoyed handling them and had the ability to present them without ever losing sight of the broader context in which these data were gathered."<ref>[https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/psychiatric-bulletin/article/eileen-m-brooke/31695230EC450E02ADD6797D057E6AA3 "Obituary: Eileen M. Brooke"], ''Psychiatric Bulletin'' No 13, 159 (1989): 159. DOI: 10.1192/pb.13.3.159</ref> Her papers are held in the Mile End Library, [[Queen Mary University of London]].<ref name=":3" />
